result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed current tracked application, deployment Bicep/scripts, settings, environment example, SQL grants, authorization setup and security-event logging. No credential values are included in outputs. Built-in LocalDB integrated authentication and UserSecretsId are not passwords. No fixed cryptographic key found. Upload rejection/errors and deletion outcomes are logged. Live cloud permissions, secret validity, ignored local files and git history were not inspected. Source-defined reproducible credentials are reported without claiming a deployed compromise.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: The SQL administrator credential is constructed at infra/main.bicep:59 from a fixed source-code password prefix and uniqueString(resourceGroup().id, environmentName), then used as administratorLoginPassword at line 68. uniqueString is a deterministic naming hash of non-secret deployment identifiers, not a cryptographic random secret; the credential is reproducible from source plus those identifiers and has no independent secret input. This is a source-defined deterministic administrator credential, not a recovered live credential. Credential text is intentionally omitted. The alternative azure-setup.sh path uses openssl randomness and is not classified as a hard-coded password.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: DetailModel.OnPostDeleteAsync accepts an arbitrary photo ID (92-96) and PhotoService.DeletePhotoAsync removes the corresponding file and database row (216-240), without checking identity or ownership. Program registers no authentication and no page authorization convention/policy, and the page model has no authorization attribute. Thus any site visitor, not just a photo owner/administrator, can obtain the publicly rendered form antiforgery token and delete any listed photo. Antiforgery validation does not assign permission to mutate another visitor's resource. This finding concerns destructive access; the public read-only gallery itself is not treated as a vulnerability. Static authorization/dataflow review; no files were deleted.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: The deployment source fixes the SQL administrator login at line 58 and determines its entire password using a fixed source prefix plus a deterministic uniqueString of the resource-group ID and environment name (59). The pair is installed as SQL administrator credentials at 67-68. Knowing the public/non-secret deployment identifiers and repository source suffices to reproduce the source-defined credential; no secret parameter, vault value, or random entropy participates in this Bicep path. Credential values are redacted from this report; no deployed account was accessed.
